text:
Maria: heads up — main CI is red after lock regen. failing DB migration test
Maria: job: https://ci.redwood/example/build/8921 (ci-bot already posted)
ci-bot: Build #8921 failed — tests/db/test_migrations.py::test_apply — exit code 1
Maria: error snippet:
```
OperationalError: could not translate host name "localhost" to address: Name or service not known
psycopg2.OperationalError: connection refused
```
Lee: is this new after the lock bump? which PR?
Maria: merged: deps/lock-2026-03-17 (poetry lock updated transitive)
Ashley: can you repro locally? maybe it's flaky in CI env
Maria: trying now, running `tox -e py39 -- tests/db/test_migrations.py::test_apply`
Maria: local fails too, same traceback
Lee: does `pip show psycopg2-binary` show a different version vs main? run `pip show psycopg2-binary`
Maria: shows 2.9.7 locally, main before bump had 2.8.6
Sam: ah — transitive pin could have pulled `psycopg2-binary` from a new build of `psycopg2` via wheel change
Ashley: think bisecting the lock commit is fastest. Maria can you bisect on the lockfile PR?
Maria: yeah I can. plan: git bisect between origin/main~5 and origin/main, run quick test script
Sam: paste script:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
pip install -q poetry
poetry install -n
pytest -q tests/db/test_migrations.py::test_apply || exit 125
exit 0
```
Lee: use exit codes 125 for bisect skip? usually 125 tells git bisect script to skip; we want 1 for fail. adjust: if fail exit 1
Sam: updated script snippet...
Maria: starting bisect now, will report offending commit
ci-bot: Note: Please include failure logs when opening a revert PR or hotfix
Ashley: thanks — if it's a transitive wheel bump we might prefer constraint pin in pyproject before reverting whole lock
Maria: bisect found commit abcdef12 — it updated `requests` to 2.31 and regen lock. suspect transitive `urllib3` bump pulled new binary wheel for psycopg2?
Lee: weird but plausible. what versions changed? Maria: `urllib3` 1.26.16 -> 2.0.6, `psycopg2-binary` 2.8.6 -> 2.9.7
Sam: for short-term: pin `psycopg2-binary==2.8.6` in pyproject.toml and regenerate lock then run CI
Ashley: or add constraint in `constraints.txt` used by CI
Maria: opening PR with pyproject pin + CI run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7145
Lee: nice. add rationale in PR body with bisect steps and logs
Maria: will do. thanks all :rocket:
